'''Victor William Guillemin''' (born 1937 in [[Boston]]) is an American [[mathematician]]. He works at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in the field of [[symplectic geometry]], and he has also made contributions to the fields of [[microlocal analysis]], [[spectral theory]], and [[mathematical physics]]. <ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Victor Guillemin {{!}} MIT Mathematics |url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=87#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |archive-url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http://math.mit.edu/directory/profile.php?pid=87#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |url-status=dead |archive-date=2007-06-15 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |title=2003 Steele Prizes |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200304/comm-steele.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=462–467}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Guillemin obtained a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] at [[Harvard University]] in 1959, as well as an [[Master of Arts|M. A.]] at the [[University of Chicago]] in 1960.<ref name=":0" /> He received a [[Ph.D.]] in mathematics from Harvard University in 1962; his dissertation, entitled ''Theory of Finite [[G-structure on a manifold|G-Structures]],'' was written under the direction of [[Shlomo Sternberg]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victor Guillemin |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=26899 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref>

He worked at [[Columbia University]] from 1963 to 1966 and then moved to the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as assistant professor. He became associate professor in 1969 and full professor in 1973.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />

==Awards and honors==
Guillemin was awarded in 1969 a [[Sloan Research Fellowship]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows Database |url=https://sloan.org/fellows-database |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]]}}</ref> in [[List of Guggenheim Fellowships awarded in 1988|1988]] a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim fellowship]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victor Guillemin |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/victor-guillemin/ |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] |language=en-US}}</ref> and in 1996 a [[Humboldt fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Victor Guillemin |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/connect/explore-the-humboldt-network/singleview?tx_rsmavhsolr_solrviewhumboldtians%5BpPersonId%5D=1040245&cHash=28ba48c942c6b6a7759d58ccf21ed931 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation]] |language=en}}</ref> In 1970 he was [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#1970, Nice|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Nice.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1970.2/ICM1970.2.ocr.pdf |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematician 1970 |publisher=Gauthier-Villars |year=1971 |editor-last= |editor-first= |volume=2 |pages=227}}</ref>

He was elected a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1984<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-07-02 |title=Victor William Guillemin |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/victor-william-guillemin |access-date=2023-07-16 |website=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] |language=en}}</ref> and of the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1985.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Victor Guillemin |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/victor-guillemin-uxchyu/ |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[United States National Academy of Sciences]]}}</ref> In 2003, he was awarded the [[Leroy P. Steele Prize]] for Lifetime Achievement by the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leroy P. Steele Prize for Lifetime Achievement (1993 - present) |url=https://www.ams.org/prizes-awards/paview.cgi?parent_id=25 |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows.cgi |access-date=2023-09-17 |website=[[American Mathematical Society]] |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
Guillemin worked in several areas in analysis and geometry, including [[microlocal analysis]], [[Symplectic geometry|symplectic]] [[Lie group action|group actions]], and [[spectral theory]] of [[Elliptic operator|elliptic operators]] on [[Manifold|manifolds]].<ref name=":0" />

He is the author or co-author of numerous books and monographs, including a widely used textbook on [[differential topology]], written jointly with Alan Pollack in 1974, and a monograph on symplectic geometry in physics, written jointly with Shlomo Sternberg in 1986.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=van Moerbeke |first=P. |author-link=Pierre van Moerbeke |date=1986 |title=Review of the book "Symplectic Techniques in Physics" by Victor Guillemin and Shlomo Sternberg |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/blms/18.6.635 |journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=18 |issue=6 |pages=635 |doi=10.1112/blms/18.6.635|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Duistermaat |first=J. J. |author-link=Hans Duistermaat |date=1988 |title=Review of the book "Symplectic techniques in physics" by Victor Guillemin and Shlomo Sternberg |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1988-18-01/S0273-0979-1988-15620-0/home.html |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |language=en |volume=18 |issue=1 |pages=97–100 |doi=10.1090/s0273-0979-1988-15620-0 |access-date=2023-09-17|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Family ==
Victor Guillemins's uncle [[Ernst Guillemin]] was a Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at MIT, his younger brother [[Sidewalk Sam|Robert Charles Guillemin]] was a sidewalk artist, his brother-in-law [[Ray Raphael]] is an historian, and his daughter [[Karen Guillemin]] is a Professor of Biology at the [[University of Oregon]].
